name: Learn: Supply Chain Security (hardened)
objective: CKS › Supply Chain Security (20%). Drill EVERY supply-chain corner harder than the exam: Trivy CVE scanning with severity gates, static manifest analysis with kubesec, digest pinning, banning :latest, ImagePullPolicy hardening, an approved-registry ValidatingAdmissionPolicy + binding, a VAP that bans :latest, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a broken binding. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Eight strict supply-chain practicals on a real cluster. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Scan an image with Trivy (severity-gated)
questions.teach:
**Trivy** scans images for known **CVEs**. Run it as a one-shot **Job** (`trivy image <ref>`) and read the `Total:` summary from the pod logs. Narrow the report with `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL` so only the CVEs that matter surface.

**Gotcha:** a Job pod must set `restartPolicy: Never` or `OnFailure` — the default `Always` is rejected.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-supply`, create a **Job** named `trivy-scan` running image `aquasec/trivy:latest` with args `image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL python:3.9.0` to scan an old Python image for HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs. Let it run to completion.

Target: Job `trivy-scan` has `succeeded >= 1`, its pod spec uses `restartPolicy: Never` (or `OnFailure`), and its logs contain Trivy CVE output (a `Total:` / `Vulnerabilities` summary).
questions.hint: `kubectl create job trivy-scan -n cks-supply --image=aquasec/trivy:latest -- image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL python:3.9.0`, then `kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/trivy-scan --timeout=240s` and read `kubectl -n cks-supply logs job/trivy-scan`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: trivy-scan
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: trivy
        image: aquasec/trivy:latest
        args: ["image","--severity","HIGH,CRITICAL","python:3.9.0"]
YAML
kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/trivy-scan --timeout=240s
kubectl -n cks-supply logs job/trivy-scan

verification.description: Job trivy-scan: completed, restartPolicy Never/OnFailure, CVE output in logs

questions.title: Static analysis with kubesec
questions.teach:
**kubesec** does **static analysis** of a Kubernetes manifest, scoring its `securityContext` hardening. It needs the YAML *inside* the container, so mount the pre-seeded ConfigMap at `/manifests` and run `scan /manifests/pod.yaml` as a Job; the logs show a JSON `score`.

**Gotcha:** the scan arg must match the mounted path (`/manifests/pod.yaml`) exactly, or kubesec errors on a missing file.
questions.prompt:
A pod manifest is mounted at `/manifests/pod.yaml` via ConfigMap `kubesec-manifest` (seeded by setup). In `cks-supply`, create a **Job** named `kubesec-scan` using image `kubesec/kubesec:latest` with args `scan /manifests/pod.yaml`, mounting that ConfigMap at `/manifests`. Let it complete.

Target: Job `kubesec-scan` has `succeeded >= 1` and its logs contain a kubesec report (a `score` field).
questions.hint: Mount the `kubesec-manifest` ConfigMap as a volume at `/manifests`; args must be `["scan","/manifests/pod.yaml"]`. Then `kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/kubesec-scan --timeout=180s` and read the logs.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: kubesec-scan
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: kubesec
        image: kubesec/kubesec:latest
        args: ["scan","/manifests/pod.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: m
          mountPath: /manifests
      volumes:
      - name: m
        configMap:
          name: kubesec-manifest
YAML
kubectl -n cks-supply wait --for=condition=complete job/kubesec-scan --timeout=180s
kubectl -n cks-supply logs job/kubesec-scan

verification.description: Job kubesec-scan completed and produced a score/report

questions.title: Pin an image by digest (@sha256:)
questions.teach:
A tag like `:1.36` is **mutable** — the registry owner can repoint it. A **digest** (`@sha256:<64 hex>`) is the hash of the exact image content, so it is **immutable**: the kubelet pulls precisely those bytes or fails. Pin with `image: busybox@sha256:<64 hex>`.

**Gotcha:** a digest is per-architecture — one copied from another arch won't pull on your node.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`, create a pod `digest-pod` (container `app`, command `sleep 3600`) whose image is pinned **by digest** — `busybox@sha256:<64-hex-digest>` (any valid busybox digest).

Target: pod `digest-pod` exists; its container image is `busybox@sha256:` followed by a 64-char hex digest (not a plain tag).
questions.hint: Find a digest with `crane digest busybox:1.36` or `docker buildx imagetools inspect busybox:1.36`, or reuse a known one. Set `image: busybox@sha256:<64-hex>`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: digest-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox@sha256:9ae97d36d26566ff84e8893c64a6dc4fe8ca6d1144bf5b87b2b85a32def253c7
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

questions.title: Ban :latest — pin a real version + imagePullPolicy
questions.teach:
`:latest` floats to whatever was pushed last, so two deploys of the "same" image can run different code. Pin an explicit tag or digest, and set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` so a pinned tag isn't silently re-pulled and swapped.

**Gotcha:** an **untagged** image (`nginx`) silently resolves to `nginx:latest` — just as bad as writing `:latest`.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`, create a **Deployment** named `web` (1 replica, container `web`) whose image is a **pinned version** — NOT `:latest`, NOT untagged. Use `nginx:1.25-alpine`, and set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` on the container.

Target: Deployment `web` exists; its container is named `web`, image carries an explicit tag (not `:latest`, not untagged) or `@sha256:`, and `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create deployment web -n cks-supply --image=nginx:1.25-alpine` names the container `nginx`, not `web` — build YAML so the container is named `web`. Add `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web } }
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.25-alpine
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
YAML

verification.description: Deployment web: container 'web', pinned image (not :latest), imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent

questions.title: Approved-registry admission (ValidatingAdmissionPolicy)
questions.teach:
A **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP)** enforces rules in-cluster with **CEL** — no webhook server. An approved-registry allowlist uses `object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))`, matched on Pods via `matchConstraints`.

**Gotcha:** the policy does **nothing** until a **binding** references it by `policyName` with `validationActions: [Deny]`.
questions.prompt:
Create a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy** `approved-registry` that denies Pods whose container images do NOT start with `registry.k8s.io/`, plus a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding** `approved-registry-binding` enabling it (action `Deny`) on Pods.

Target: both objects exist; the policy's CEL validation references `registry.k8s.io` over `object.spec.containers`; the binding has `policyName: approved-registry` and `validationActions` containing `Deny`.
questions.hint: `matchConstraints.resourceRules` on resource `pods` (apiGroups `[""]`). Validation CEL: `object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))`. Binding: `policyName: approved-registry`, `validationActions: [Deny]`, `matchResources: {}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: approved-registry
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE","UPDATE"]
      resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))"
    message: "images must come from registry.k8s.io"
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: approved-registry-binding
spec:
  policyName: approved-registry
  validationActions: ["Deny"]
  matchResources: {}
YAML

verification.description: VAP approved-registry + binding with the registry.k8s.io rule and Deny

questions.title: Ban :latest cluster-wide with a VAP
questions.teach:
The same VAP mechanism can **ban `:latest`**: a CEL check `object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))` rejects any Pod whose container image ends in `:latest`. It pairs with its own binding, independent of the registry policy.

**Gotcha:** this does NOT catch an untagged image (`nginx`) — `endsWith(':latest')` is false for it; catching that needs a stricter CEL (`c.image.contains(':') || c.image.contains('@')`).
questions.prompt:
Create a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy** `no-latest-tag` that denies Pods with a container image ending in `:latest`, plus a binding `no-latest-tag-binding` enabling it (action `Deny`) on Pods.

Target: both objects exist; the policy's CEL validation references `:latest` with `endsWith` over `object.spec.containers`; the binding has `policyName: no-latest-tag` and `validationActions` containing `Deny`.
questions.hint: Validation CEL: `object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))`. Then a binding with `policyName: no-latest-tag`, `validationActions: [Deny]`, `matchResources: {}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: no-latest-tag
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE","UPDATE"]
      resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))"
    message: "the :latest tag is banned"
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: no-latest-tag-binding
spec:
  policyName: no-latest-tag
  validationActions: ["Deny"]
  matchResources: {}
YAML

verification.description: VAP no-latest-tag + binding banning :latest with Deny

questions.title: Private-registry pull via imagePullSecrets
questions.teach:
Images from a private registry need credentials: create a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret with `kubectl create secret docker-registry`, then reference it under the pod spec's `imagePullSecrets`. The kubelet uses it to authenticate the pull.

**Gotcha:** `imagePullSecrets` lives on the **pod spec** (`spec.imagePullSecrets`), not on the container — and the Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`: (1) create a docker-registry Secret `regcred` for server `registry.internal:5000`, username `ci`, password `s3cr3t`; (2) create pod `private-pod` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`) that references `regcred` under `spec.imagePullSecrets`.

Target: Secret `regcred` is type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`; pod `private-pod` lists `regcred` in `spec.imagePullSecrets`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t`. Then in the pod spec add `imagePullSecrets: [ { name: regcred } ]`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: private-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  imagePullSecrets:
  - name: regcred
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

verification.description: regcred dockerconfigjson Secret + private-pod referencing it in imagePullSecrets

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a VAP binding that enforces nothing
questions.teach:
A **ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding** is inert unless its `policyName` names a real policy AND `validationActions` includes `Deny`. Inspect with `kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding <b> -o yaml` and compare `policyName` to the actual policy name and the action.

**Gotcha:** a binding pointing at a non-existent policy is accepted silently — it just never enforces, so bad Pods sail through.
questions.prompt:
A policy `block-privileged` exists, but its binding `block-privileged-binding` (seeded by setup) **enforces nothing** — privileged Pods are still admitted. Diagnose why and fix the binding so it actually enforces `block-privileged` with action `Deny`. Don't delete and recreate from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: binding `block-privileged-binding` has `policyName: block-privileged` and `validationActions` containing `Deny`.
questions.hint: `kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding -o yaml` — the `policyName` points at a wrong/typo'd policy and/or `validationActions` isn't `Deny`. Patch it: `kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"policyName":"block-privileged","validationActions":["Deny"]}}'`.
questions.solution:
# The seeded binding references a wrong policyName and action Warn — it enforces nothing.
kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"policyName":"block-privileged","validationActions":["Deny"]}}'

verification.description: block-privileged-binding now targets block-privileged with Deny
